Article Title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day leaked on X, reached 5.9 million accounts, and then…
Article Text:
5.9 million accounts saw the Spider-Man leak on X. Sony still had a record Friday.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day

The Odyssey last week, Spider-Man this week: How X keeps ending up as the internet's biggest movie leak platform

The Odyssey

Spider-Man: Brand New Day box office records survived the piracy anyway

Brand New Day

Avengers: Endgame

Endgame

Endgame

Spider-Man: No Way Home

A high-quality bootleg ofsat in plain sight on X for most of Friday, reaching 5.9 million accounts before Sony managed to get it pulled. The post went up at 6:05 am PT from an account calling itself Fredrick Bryan, early enough that plenty of people in the US saw the film before their local matinee started. It stayed live until roughly 3:25 pm PT, by which point it had collected more than 143,000 likes and over 10,000 reshares.Copies surfaced on other accounts through the day, though most lasted only minutes. Clips spoiling the film's biggest reveals spread faster than the full rip and proved harder to contain, with many of those posts now replaced by a copyright-disabled notice. Sony declined to comment.This is the second time in eight days that a major release has been dumped on X in full. A three-hour rip of Christopher Nolan'swent up last weekend, pulled 2.1 million views in two and a half hours, and ended with the account suspended. Universal said it moved to takedown protocols as soon as it spotted the upload and would chase every remedy available to protect its copyright.The mechanics are simple enough. Since Elon Musk's 2022 rebrand, X Premium subscribers have been able to upload videos up to four hours long, which is comfortably more runway than most tentpoles need.None of it slowed the film down.took $72 million in previews, including Tuesday early-access screenings, beating the $60 millionmanaged in 2019. Friday's opening day landed at roughly $168 million with previews folded in, ahead of's $157.4 million.Sony is guiding conservatively at $325 million for the weekend.'s $357 million still stands as the domestic record, withsecond at $260 million.Tom Holland returns as Peter Parker alongside Zendaya's MJ, with Sadie Sink in a role Sony has worked hard to keep under wraps, plus Jon Bernthal and Jacob Batalon. IGN scored it 7/10.The leak was enormous by any normal measure. It just happened to run into a weekend where several million people paid for a ticket regardless.
Article Summary: 5.9 million accounts saw the Spider-Man leak on X. Sony still had a record Friday. A three-hour rip of Christopher Nolan'swent up last weekend, pulled 2.1 million views in two and a half hours. Universal said it moved to takedown protocols as soon as it spotted the upload.

Article Title: Donald Trump on Minnesota water system attack: Not Iran, I blame it on Minnesota as they are grossly incompetent
Article Text:
Donald Trump

Donald Trump's remarks differ from reports citing investigators

Federal agencies continue investigation

Minnesota's water systems recently came under a cyberattack, with US officials reportedly suspecting that the operation was carried out by Iran. However, US President Donald Trump disagrees. According to a report by news agency Reuters, while speaking to reporters at Camp David, Trump dismissed the suggestion that Tehran was responsible for the attacks.During a Cabinet meeting,Trump said, “We heard in Minnesota there was a cyberattack, and they blame it on Iran. I don't think so.” He then added, "I think I blame it on Minnesota because they're grossly incompetent," referring to Minnesota Governor Tim Walz, who is a Democrat. It's important to note that Trump did not reveal who he believed was actually responsible for the cyberattacks.Responding to Trump’s remarks, Minnesota Governor Tim Walz shared a post on X saying, "Trump knows exactly who is responsible for this attack, and knows that other states were hit too."Walz also criticised Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), writing that it "took an axe to CISA and left the US exposed to cyberattacks," while thanking cybersecurity experts in Minnesota for identifying the vulnerability and helping local communities contain the incident.According to the Reuters report, Trump's comments differ from information cited by Wired, which reported that a memo from the Minnesota Fusion Center said the July 26 and 27 cyberattacks were "aligned" with an allegedly Iran-linked cyber sabotage campaign.The New York Times, citing unnamed US and state officials, also reported that investigators believed the attacks were probably carried out by Tehran. However, the report noted that no federal or state agency has formally attributed responsibility for the attacks.The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) told Reuters earlier this week that it is coordinating with the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and other government and industry partners to determine the scope of the attacks and provide support.Separately, the FBI said it had received reports of similar cyber incidents affecting water facilities in at least seven US states since July 27. According to an advisory issued by the bureau, some of the attacks have "degraded water operations."This week, the FBI said that it is aware of public reporting about the incidents and is working with partner agencies to protect critical infrastructure."…we remain well-equipped to protect against cyber threats of all varieties," the agency said in a statement.Cybersecurity experts point to similarities with earlier attacksAs per the report, cybersecurity experts and Minnesota's state IT agency said the attacks share characteristics with hacking activity targeting water infrastructure that seven US government agencies, which include the FBI, NSA, EPA and CISA, linked to Iranian-affiliated hackers in a July 22 advisory.The advisory warned that hackers associated with Iran had targeted critical water facility equipment, although officials have not formally connected the Minnesota incidents to those earlier attacks.
Article Summary: Minnesota's water systems recently came under a cyberattack. US officials reportedly suspect that the operation was carried out by Iran. However, US President Donald Trump disagrees. Trump said, "I think I blame it on Minnesota because they're grossly incompetent," referring to Minnesota Governor Tim Walz, who is a Democrat.

Article Title: Crypto company CEO stole $5 million from his own company, erased 194 expense records and then abruptly resigned
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation purpose only

Bitquery lawsuit alleges CEO transferred company funds to personal accounts

Former Bitquery CEO allegedly deleted 194 financial records before resigning

CEO and co-founder of cryptocurrency data company Bitquery has been accused of stealing more than $5 million from the business before deleting nearly 200 financial records and abruptly resigning. Dionysios “Dean” Karakitsos, 57, allegedly transferred company funds to accounts linked to himself and his associates over several years, according to a lawsuit filed by Bitquery in Manhattan Supreme Court. The lawsuit further claims Karakitsos, who left the company in October 2025, allegedly deleted 194 expense and bill records from its accounting system.According to the lawsuit, the alleged scheme began around 2022, when investors put about $8 million into Bitquery. The company tracks cryptocurrency prices, transactions and flows. Karakitsos allegedly had sole control over Bitquery’s financial accounts. The lawsuit claims he used that access to transfer money to several entities operated by him and his associates, including an entity based in the UK.Bitquery also accused its former CEO of giving investors a misleading picture of the company’s financial position. Karakitsos allegedly told investors that the company had between $5 million and $6 million in the bank.However, according to the lawsuit, Bitquery generated about $2 million in revenue and had roughly similar operating expenses in 2024 and 2025.The lawsuit claims Karakitsos tried to hide the alleged transfers shortly before resigning in October 2025. He allegedly deleted 194 expense entries and bill records from Bitquery’s QuickBooks accounting system. The company claims those records showed transfers of money into his personal accounts. He is also accused of changing other records to conceal the transactions.Bitquery further alleges that Karakitsos continues to hold banking credentials belonging to the company and has refused to return them.“The harm to Bitquery is substantial, ongoing, and aggravated by each day that Karakitsos retains exclusive control over the Company’s accounts,” the filing stated.Bitquery filed the lawsuit in June and is seeking the return of at least $5 million that it claims was misappropriated. The company is also seeking additional damages, banking credentials, a full accounting of the funds and property allegedly purchased using company money. Bitquery has since appointed co-founder Aleksey Studnev as its CEO.Karakitsos has denied the allegations. “I strongly disagree with the allegations and intend to respond through the legal process,” he said.
Article Summary: Former Bitquery CEO allegedly deleted 194 financial records before resigning. Dionysios “Dean” Karakitsos, 57, allegedly transferred company funds to accounts linked to himself and his associates over several years. Bitquery filed the lawsuit in June and is seeking the return of at least $5 million.

Article Title: After layoffs in AGI division, shutdown of Lab, Amazon is reorganizing teams and refocusing its AI strategy
Article Text:
Amazon changing AI strategy, says report.

Amazon is ‘killing’ flagship models



What Amazon has to say



Amazon’s AI roboticist to head frontier model research



Amazon is shaking things up in its artificial intelligence (AI) division. Those changes include winding down a number of flagship in-house models, closing down specialized research groups, and consolidating its engineering talent behind a pared-down frontier-model effort. The shift comes on the heels of recent layoffs within Amazon's Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) organisation and the complete shutdown of AGI Lab, which was a high-profile research unit formed in 2024 following the acquisition of key talent from AI startup Adept.According to a report by Business Insider, instead of spreading resources across multiple text, image and video generation projects, the tech giant is redirecting compute power and technical staff toward a single primary initiative designed to keep pace with industry rivals.Citing internal sources, the report says that Amazon has begun ‘deprecating’ several prominent models from its Nova lineup. These include high-end Premier and Omni models, the Reel video generator and the Canvas image generator.The sources describe these systems to the publication as shifting into a “keep the lights on” (KTLO) state, which is a technical designation, meaning the software remains active for existing enterprise clients but will no longer receive active development or feature updates.The remaining Nova suite will continue to maintain select lightweight and task-specific offerings, including the Nova 2 Sonic and Nova 2 Lite models, alongside Nova Forge for model customisation and Nova Act for AI agent development, the report noted.In a statement addressing the portfolio changes, an Amazon spokesperson told BI that model evolution reflects standard lifecycle management:“AI models remain one of the most important things we're working on, and that hasn't changed. As with any AI portfolio, we continually evolve our model lineup based on what customers need, and we always provide customers clear guidance and migration paths as models advance," the spokesperson was quoted as saying.Engineering priorities and hardware resources are now consolidating under Frontier Model Research (FMR), an initiative led by renowned AI roboticist Pieter Abbeel, who joined Amazon via its acquisition of Covariant. Under Abbeel's leadership, FMR is tasked with building Amazon's next-generation foundation model, which is expected to debut at the company’s annual re:Invent conference.
Article Summary: Report: Amazon is winding down flagship in-house models, closing down specialized research groups, and consolidating its engineering talent behind a pared-down frontier-model effort. The shift comes on the heels of recent layoffs within Amazon's Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) organisation.

Article Title: The world’s largest digital camera captured more than 500,000 galaxies and 50,000 stars in one deep view of the universe
Article Text:
Rubin Observatory stacked hundreds of images from its 3.2-billion-pixel camera; the final view contains over half a million galaxies and 50,000 stars. (NSF–DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory:NOIRLab:SLAC:AURA)

How the image was made



Why astronomers keep returning to this exact patch of sky



What Rubin adds to the picture



Astronomers have just got their clearest look yet at one of the most studied patches of sky in the world. The Vera C. Rubin Observatory, based in Chile, has released a single stacked image containing more than 500,000 galaxies and over 50,000 stars, captured using the largest digital camera ever built. Here’s all the information on how the photo has been captured and the significance of this cosmic milestone.The image comes from Rubin's 3.2-gigapixel (3.2-billion-pixel) LSST Camera, mounted on the observatory’s 8.4-meter Simonyi Survey Telescope. Instead of a single snapshot, the photograph was built by stacking hundreds of individual images on top of each other, layering exposure over exposure until faint, distant light became visible.The result is a single frame which is packed with spiral galaxies with arms, smooth elliptical galaxies, galaxies caught mid-collision and faint red galaxies from the far reaches of the early universe. Only a small number of bright stars from our own Milky Way sit in the foreground, which is actually part of what makes the image so striking.Rubin Observatory is a joint project funded by the US National Science Foundation and the US Department of Energy’s Office of Science.The region captured in this image is known as the COSMOS field. Astronomers have been studying it for more than two decades, starting with observations from the Hubble Space Telescope back in 2003. Since then, researchers have pointed many of the world's most powerful telescopes at the same patch of sky, gathering data across everything from radio waves to X-rays.What makes COSMOS so useful is its location. It sits away from the crowded plane of our own galaxy, meaning there’s less interference from nearby stars, and dust clouds blocking the view. That gives telescopes an unusually clean line of sight to enormous numbers of distant galaxies. Scientists say that some are so far away that their light has been travelling toward Earth for billions of years.As looking farther into space is also accepted as a means of looking further back in time, this field lets scientists study galaxies at many different points in the universe’s history, essentially within one continuous dataset.Rubin's contribution to this field is a mix of depth, wide coverage and repetition. By photographing COSMOS again and again over time, the observatory builds a dynamic record of how the sky itself changes. That’s a key part of Rubin's broader mission: a ten-year survey called the Legacy Survey of Space and Time, or LSST, designed to create the most detailed, continuously updated record of the universe ever attempted.Due to its scientific importance, future observations are expected to reveal fainter galaxies and sharper details than what's visible today.Further, this image marks Rubin's Early Data Preview 2, or EDP2 — the observatory's first data release built specifically from LSST Camera observations. It combines science validation data collected between April 2025 and January 2026, and covers roughly 3,000 square degrees of night sky, or about one-sixth of the entire visible Southern Hemisphere.Bob Blum, Director of Rubin Observatory at NSF NOIRLab, said the COSMOS image marks just the beginning of what the field will offer. He said that repeated visits to the region over the coming years are expected to uncover large numbers of short-lived cosmic events, such as supernovae, that scientists can follow up on and study in detail.
Article Summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory, based in Chile, has released a single stacked image containing more than 500,000 galaxies and over 50,000 stars. The region captured in this image is known as the COSMOS field. Astronomers have been studying it for more than two decades, starting with observations from the Hubble Space Telescope in 2003.

Article Title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says he got addicted to this ‘Larry Ellison’s app’; It got ‘too powerful’ for him
Article Text:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman compared the experience to a drug

TikTok ownership change in the US

The rise and fall of OpenAI's Sora app

Even Sam Altman is not immune to the endless scrolling on TikTok. The OpenAI CEO recently revealed that he forced himself to get “addicted” to TikTok to study its mechanics only to delete the app after finding it “too powerful” to control. Speaking on a recent episode of the Relentless podcast, Altman shared how a research experiment to understand TikTok’s recommendation algorithm quickly spiraled into a personal distraction.“I made myself get addicted to TikTok, because I wanted to just learn. I really thought it was great. “And then I thought I could control it. I was like, 'Oh, it's actually kind of fun,' but I only use it for 10 minutes to wind down before bed, and I'm totally in control of it. And then it was an hour one night. And then some Saturday afternoon, I was on the couch for like three hours,” Altman said.Altman compared the experience to a drug, noting that while he was “really enjoying it in the moment,” he knew the habit was bad for him. After briefly scaling his usage down to a few minutes before bed, he decided to delete the app entirely.“I briefly got it back under control, and I was down to five, 10 minutes a night, whatever, like a little wind down before bed,” he said, adding, “Then I was just like, enough.”After years of deliberation, TikTok’s US operations are now owned by a majority-investor entity called TikTok USDS Joint Venture that includes Larry Ellison’s Oracle, Silver Lake and MGX. The global operations, however, remain tied to ByteDance, which retains a minority 19.9% share in the US venture. Meanwhile, the storage and algorithmic operations in the US are hosted securely on Oracle cloud infrastructure.Altman’s deep dive into TikTok coincided with OpenAI’s internal efforts to build its own AI-generated video social media platform, Sora. Despite generating massive hype and securing a partnership with Disney, OpenAI officially scrapped the Sora app project in March after six months of development.Company executives determined that rendering video consumed too much computing power at a time when resources were better spent competing with rivals like Anthropic in the core generative AI race.
Article Summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says he got addicted to TikTok to study its mechanics. Altman compared the experience to a drug, noting that while he was “really enjoying it in the moment,” he knew the habit was bad for him. After briefly scaling his usage down, he decided to delete the app entirely.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg is not convinced if OpenAI and Anthropic really want Chinese AI models in America, says: Signal is ...
Article Text:
The increasing Chinese competition



Open vs closed models



Mark Zuckerberg makes an offer to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei



Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has entered the intensifying Washington debate over whether Chinese AI models should be restricted in the US, wanting that banning them would not be ‘an effective solution’. In an interview with Financial Times, Zuckerberg said the US should compete by identifying bottlenecks and roadblocks rather than blocking rivals outright. He also cautioned against ‘regulatory capture’ by American frontier labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic, which he suggested could use policy to throttle domestic competition. Zuckerberg’s remarks appeared to be a broadside against OpenAI and Anthropic, which dominate the chatbot market with proprietary closed models. He said there were “mixed signals” about whether frontier labs truly want open-source models to succeed. “Are the frontier labs going to want an open-source model to succeed? I think that there have kind of been some mixed signals on that,” he told the FT.The comments from Zuckerberg comes after Beijing-based Moonsht AI released its Kimi K3 model, whose capabilities are nearing those of OpenAI and Anthropic. US officials have also accused Moonshot of covertly training its model using distillation from American rivals, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warning that sanctions are on the table for labs that cross into intellectual property theft.Zuckerberg reiterated his support for “AI for everyone” and open models that users can customize and run on their own hardware — a popular approach among Chinese developers. He warned that AI risks becoming centralized in the hands of a few powerful groups. While Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has called for stronger regulation and Google DeepMind’s Demis Hassabis has proposed a self-regulatory body, Zuckerberg said restrictions on powerful tools were not the right answer. He argued that open models could help patch cybersecurity vulnerabilities faster than closed ones.Zuckerberg’s intervention highlights a growing split among U.S. tech leaders over how to respond to Chinese competition and regulate AI. While rivals push for tighter controls, he is positioning Meta as a champion of open-source approaches — even as his company develops its own closed model, Muse Spark, citing safety concerns.In related news, recently it was reported that Meta is in early talks to lease computing power to Anthropic in a deal that could be worth as much as $10 billion over two years, according to a New York Times report. If it closes, it would hand Mark Zuckerberg a brand-new line of business and pull Dario Amodei's AI lab deeper into a scramble for compute that shows no sign of easing.The move borrows straight from Elon Musk's playbook. Musk turned SpaceX's Colossus data centers into a rental business earlier this year, and Anthropic became its anchor tenant. Now Zuckerberg wants a slice of the same action, using the very data centers his investors keep grumbling about. Anthropic pitched the idea first, in JuneThe NYT reports that Anthropic proposed the deal in June, and Meta is weighing it. Anthropic would pay in monthly instalments across two years, with either side free to opt out early. The specifics are still moving around.
Article Summary: Zuckerberg says US should compete by identifying bottlenecks and roadblocks rather than blocking rivals outright. Warns against ‘regulatory capture’ by American frontier labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic, which he suggested could use policy to throttle domestic competition.

Article Title: Nvidia in talks with OpenAI to guarantee $250B for US' biggest data center project that also has Japan's 'promise'
Article Text:
How Nvidia’s guarantee could help OpenAI secure financing



Campus expected to require 10 gigawatts of power



Japan's investment is tied to US trade agreement



AI companies race to secure power and infrastructure



Nvidia is reportedly in talks with OpenAI to provide a $250 billion financial guarantee for what could become the largest data center project announced in the US. According to a report by The Wall Street Journal, the proposed arrangement would support OpenAI's plans to lease a massive AI data center campus in southern Ohio being developed by SB Energy, which is backed by Japan’s biggest company, SoftBank.The project even carries a significant international component. As part of a recent US-Japan trade agreement, Japan has committed $33 billion to fund a natural gas power project that will supply electricity to the site, while the US government controls the allocation of power. According to the report, US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is also involved in deciding which companies receive access to the power generated at the facility.The report cited people familiar with the matter as saying that Nvidia's proposed guarantee would help reassure lenders financing the project, because OpenAI is currently an unprofitable private company and lacks an investment-grade credit rating. The guarantee would cover financing linked to the data center lease and construction debt, but not the Nvidia chips that will power the facility.The report added that Nvidia is separately discussing financing the purchase of AI chips for OpenAI, a deal that could total $350 billion.The terms of both agreements have not been finalised, and discussions could still fall through.The proposed campus would require approximately 10 gigawatts of electricity, which is enough to supply several million homes and would be built over multiple years. The report notes that the first phase is expected to be completed in 2028, initially providing around 800 megawatts of computing capacity.The overall project, including Nvidia's AI chips, could eventually cost more than $500 billion, making it the largest announced AI data center development to date.The Ohio project is linked to a broader US-Japan economic agreement announced earlier this year. As part of the arrangement, Japan agreed to invest $33 billion in a natural gas-powered energy project on federal land in Ohio. The facility will be operated by SB Energy, which is effectively controlled by SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son.According to the report, the US government will pay SB Energy a fee to operate the power plant, while the US and Japan will share electricity revenues until Japan recovers its investment. After that, the US government is expected to receive 90% of the revenue generated. Construction of the project officially began in March, when Lutnick, Son and US Energy Secretary Chris Wright attended the groundbreaking ceremony.OpenAI is among several companies interested in leasing the Ohio campus. According to The Wall Street Journal, Anthropic, Microsoft and Google have also discussed the project with Lutnick in recent weeks.The development reflects increasing competition among AI companies to secure access to computing power, specialised chips and electricity needed to train and operate large AI models.The Ohio campus would also mark OpenAI's first large-scale data center as a tenant, reducing its reliance on cloud providers such as Microsoft, Amazon and Oracle for AI infrastructure.The report noted that OpenAI recently increased its projected spending on computing infrastructure to around $750 billion through 2030, up from an earlier estimate of approximately $600 billion.For Nvidia, the proposed guarantee could further strengthen demand for its AI chips. However, the company previously disclosed in its annual report that financing arrangements supporting customers' data center projects could increase its exposure to credit risk while reducing near-term cash flows.
Article Summary: OpenAI is reportedly in talks with Nvidia to provide a $250 billion financial guarantee for what could become the largest data center project in the US. The proposed arrangement would support OpenAI's plans to lease a massive AI data center campus in southern Ohio. Japan has committed $33 billion to fund a natural gas power project that will supply electricity to the site.

Article Title: After laying off 20% employees, one of world's biggest creator platforms wants rest of staff back in office
Article Text:
Return to office strengthens connection



Patreon refocusing under AI and rising competition



Patreon, one of the world's largest creator membership platforms, is tightening its return-to-office policy just days after cutting its workforce by 20%. According to a report by Business Insider, the company notified employees that it is raising its in-office requirement from two days to three days a week for staff assigned to its three main hubs in New York City, San Francisco and Porto in Portugal.The report says that the announcement was made to remaining staff a day after Patreon laid off 93 employees. A company spokesperson confirmed the shift to the publication, noting that the updated policy will roll out in the coming months and will not affect employees who are already officially classified as remote workers.Patreon refers to its in-office policy internally as “Time Together.” In a statement, the company defended the mandate as a way to improve collaboration following the staff reductions.“Since returning to two days a week in-office, we’ve been able to build stronger connections across the team. We're making this change to spend more intentional in-person time together to continue strengthening the feeling of community and togetherness we have at Patreon,” a Patreon spokesperson was quoted as saying.The move mirrors a broader trend across major tech and media companies seeking to rebuild in-office work culture.Companies like Instagram and TikTok have also pushed stricter attendance policies, with select teams required to be in the office up to five days a week.Historically, Patreon’s approach to office attendance has been relatively flexible. Former employees noted that the platform required staff to meet a 75% attendance threshold on designated days, allowing workers to miss roughly one out of every four required office days without penalty.Additionally, several employees living within commuting distance were previously granted remote status, exempting them from attendance rules.The combination of job cuts and stricter office rules comes as Patreon restructures its organisation to move faster. In an internal memo sent to employees, Patreon CEO Jack Conte pointed to technological change and the rise of artificial intelligence (AI) as key factors driving the company’s reorganisation.“AI has fundamentally transformed the tech industry, the pace of change has never been more intense, and I expect it to get even faster,” Conte wrote, highlighting that Patreon needs “increased agility” to adapt to market shifts.
Article Summary: Patreon is raising its in-office requirement from two days to three days a week. The move comes just days after the company laid off 93 employees. The company says the move will improve collaboration and build community. It will not affect employees who are already officially classified as remote workers.

Article Title: Microsoft updates its Insider Trading policy and has a message for employees to stop using these platforms
Article Text:
Rise of prediction markets

Microsoft CFO Amy Hood's email to employees has a message on the company's biggest AI bets

Microsoft has updated its General Insider Trading Policy to explicitly include ‘prediction markets and event contacts’. According to a report by Business Insider, in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the tech giant has warned the employees that trading on such platforms using confidential information is prohibited under securities laws and Microsoft’s own rules. The updated policy states: “You may not participate in third-party platforms, ‘prediction markets,’ or similar platforms to bet, wager, or establish positions in event contracts when such activity is based on, or involves the use of, confidential information about Microsoft or any other company (including customers, vendors, or partners of Microsoft or an economically-linked company such as a competitor of Microsoft) obtained through your position at Microsoft.”Microsoft’s move aligns with growing scrutiny of prediction markets, though its policy is not as restrictive as some Wall Street banks. Goldman Sachs, for example, has banned employees from participating in contracts linked to financial markets or political events. Still, Microsoft’s broad language suggests the company wants employees to steer clear of any activity that could expose them to insider trading risks across its diverse business ecosystem.Platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket have surged in popularity, offering trades on real-world outcomes ranging from corporate earnings calls to global events. Kalshi recently recorded more than $27 billion in trades tied to the 2026 World Cup. During Microsoft’s latest earnings call, both platforms offered contracts on which words or phrases executives would use.Federal regulators and the Department of Justice have begun cracking down on suspected insider trading in prediction markets. In May, a Google engineer was charged after allegedly using confidential company information to make over $1 million on Polymarket. More recently, a White House teleprompter operator was put on leave after reportedly netting $100,000 on Kalshi.Microsoft CFO Amy Hood told employees that the company’s biggest AI investments are paying off, citing string growth in Azure and momentum for Copilot. According to a report by Business Insider, in her quarterly memo following earnings, Hood emphasised that these businesses are showing ‘important progress’ even as Microsoft spends tens of billions to expand data center capacity and keep pace in the AI race. Microsoft report $90 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, surpassing Wall Street forecasts. Cloud revenue reached $59.3 billion in Q4 and $214 billion for the fiscal year, growing 27%. Azure revenue growth accelerated to 43%, with the cloud business surpassing $100 billion annually. Copilot adoption also surged, with net paid seat adds more than doubling sequentially to over 30 million.Hood also added that Microsoft’s $41 billion in capital expenditures during the quarter to expand infrastructure, thanking engineering and infrastructure teams for efficiencies that maximize capacity. She reiterated that security remains a top priority, stressing that customer trust is earned daily through reliability and quality. Other highlights included $19.6 billion in free cash flow, 16% growth in Microsoft 365 commercial cloud revenue, and 24% growth in consumer cloud revenue. LinkedIn revenue rose 12%, while Xbox content and services fell 10% compared to a strong prior-year quarter. Windows OEM and Devices revenue decreased 7%, reflecting inventory adjustments by partners.In closing, Hood praised teams for discipline and commitment, noting that Microsoft’s success depends on creating meaningful value for customers. “We begin this new year with clear priorities, strong customer demand, and significant opportunity ahead. At the same time, capturing the opportunity in front of us will require us to continue evolving, raising our ambition, and finding new ways to deliver for our customers,” she wrote.
Article Summary: Microsoft has updated its General Insider Trading Policy to explicitly include ‘prediction markets and event contacts’ The tech giant has warned the employees that trading on such platforms using confidential information is prohibited under securities laws and Microsoft’s own rules. Move aligns with growing scrutiny of prediction markets.

Article Title: As MIT spends $3 million on 500 AI cameras, students question facial recognition and campus surveillance
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation

More than 500 AI cameras planned across campus

Cameras use AI for real-time detection

Students raise privacy concerns

"History has shown us that surveillance states exist not to protect innocent people from criminals, but to make criminals of innocent people,"

"We have seen this phenomenon play out at MIT, where the ratcheting up of tracking systems and police presence over the past years have done little other for the community than assist in witch hunts against student protestors."

"I understand the motivation behind [the new cameras], but I am not convinced that many more cameras in the hallway is useful in preventing anything. Seeing cameras everywhere I go makes me uncomfortable," E

Expansion comes during budget cuts

Massachusetts Institute of Technology ( MIT ) is reportedly spending more than $3 million to install over 500 AI-powered surveillance cameras across its campus as part of a multi-phase security expansion. While the university says the project is intended to improve campus safety, students have raised concerns over facial recognition capabilities, expanded surveillance and how the collected data could be used.According to MIT's student newspaper, The Tech, these new cameras will be capable of real-time face and object classification, including detection of motion, crowds, face masks, and other attributes. Defending the rollout, MIT spokesperson Kimberly Allen said the cameras are "part of regular efforts to promote campus security," adding that the data collected is "retained up to 30 days" unless an exception is granted.According to documents reviewed by The Tech, installation of the new surveillance system began in November 2025 and is expected to continue through September 2026.The project includes 521 AI-integrated cameras across academic buildings, residence halls and outdoor locations along Memorial Drive.Of these, 501 are single-lens cameras, and 20 are quad-lens models capable of monitoring multiple directions simultaneously.The expansion will also add 67 exterior cameras and 13 new "Code Blue" emergency phone towers, each equipped with surveillance cameras, public address systems, emergency lighting and pan-tilt-zoom cameras.Most of the project's nearly $2 million camera contract has been awarded to Siemens, while telecommunications contractors LCN and Picardi Electric are handling installation, wiring and related infrastructure work.The primary camera supplier is Hanwha Vision, whose Wisenet AI cameras use deep learning algorithms to identify and classify people, vehicles, and other objects in real time.According to technical specifications cited by The Tech, the cameras can detect facial features, licence plates, motion, loitering, crowds, camera tampering and objects such as bags and vehicles. They can also classify individuals based on clothing colour, gender and estimated age from distances of up to 35 feet (11 metres).Nearly all cameras will support pan, tilt, rotate, and zoom functions and will be continuously monitored using AI-RGUS, an AI-powered surveillance monitoring platform.Allen said the cameras' audio recording functions have been disabled, noting that state law prohibits audio surveillance.Some MIT students questioned whether the expanded surveillance could be used beyond campus security. Evan Lofink '27 expressed concern that the system could be used to monitor student demonstrations.Lofink said.Jayna Ekelmann '27 said she understood the reasons behind the project but questioned its effectiveness.kelmann said.The surveillance project comes as MIT continues to implement budget reductions triggered by federal funding changes, including hiring freezes, salary freezes and the closure of multiple campus libraries.According to The Tech, the camera rollout reflects a broader trend among US universities expanding surveillance infrastructure. The University of Pennsylvania has increased its outdoor camera network over the past five years, while Brown University has also announced plans to expand campus surveillance following a fatal shooting in December.Allen said MIT's surveillance expansion was already underway before the December 2025 shooting of Professor Nuno Loureiro and was not initiated in response to that incident or the shooting at Brown University.MIT said the AI camera project is the first phase of a broader campus surveillance expansion, although details of future phases have not yet been disclosed.
Article Summary: Massachusetts Institute of Technology is reportedly spending more than $3 million to install over 500 AI-powered surveillance cameras across its campus. The cameras will be capable of real-time face and object classification, including detection of motion, crowds, face masks, and other attributes. Students have raised concerns over facial recognition capabilities, expanded surveillance and how the collected data could be used.

Article Title: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg predicts billions will have a personal AI agent working in next five years

Mark Zuckerberg

Mark Zuckerberg sees WhatsApp playing a key role in AI agents



Meta bets on AI despite rising infrastructure spending

Article Title: Quote of the day by Bill Gates: “Power comes not from knowledge kept but…” - a timeless lesson that still resonates
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Bill Gates



“Power comes not from knowledge kept but from knowledge shared.”

What the quote means



How collective learning drives progress



About Bill Gates



Other notable quotes by Bill Gates



"Success is a lousy teacher. It seduces smart people into thinking they can't lose."

"Your most unhappy customers are your greatest source of learning."

"I choose a lazy person to do a hard job because a lazy person will find an easy way to do it."

"Patience is a key element of success."

Lessons that can be applied in everyday life



Why the idea remains relevant



A common misunderstanding



Idea has always been a driving force behind the development of society; however, its true power can be unleashed only after dissemination. It can be either scientific discovery, teaching or simply some valuable information exchanged by peers. Information never gets to realize its full potential if it stays solely with one person. This idea lies behind the following Quote of the Day by Bill Gates, who said: "Power comes not from knowledge hoarded, but from knowledge shared."The founder of Microsoft has always been talking about innovations, education and solutions of world problems through collaboration. His words emphasise that only sharing knowledge can give an expert an opportunity to make his contribution to the development of other people, improvement of current concepts and creation of something new.At its simplest, the statement draws a distinction between possessing information and putting it to wider use. Knowing something can improve an individual's decisions, but sharing that knowledge allows many more people to benefit from it.This does not mean every piece of information should always be public. Certain knowledge must remain confidential because of privacy, security or legal responsibilities. The quote speaks more broadly about education, research, experience and ideas that help society move forward.Someone who teaches a skill, explains a difficult concept or documents a useful process creates opportunities that extend beyond their own work. In that sense, influence comes not only from expertise but from making expertise accessible.This principle also takes into consideration the fact that most of the time advancement comes about in steps, and not as individual inventions. Scientists make inventions based on earlier works. Engineers make improvements on previous work. Teachers teach knowledge from one generation to another. All these writers, painters and scholars draw their inspiration from other sources.The sharing of information does not devalue the idea for the originator of the knowledge. Contrary to material property, information does not become lost as soon as it has been given out to another person. In some cases, as other people add their own experiences, the initial idea may even gain some strength in the process.However, there is an additional dimension to the whole thing. Open dialogue leads to mistakes being questioned. Theories tested out by many individuals tend to evolve faster than theories which have only been created by a few individuals.Bill Gates co-founded Microsoft in 1975 alongside Paul Allen, helping to transform personal computing from a specialist field into part of everyday life. During his years at Microsoft, he became known for his focus on software, long-term technological trends and the rapid expansion of personal computers.In later years, Gates shifted much of his attention towards philanthropy through the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. The foundation has supported programmes in global health, disease prevention, agriculture, education and poverty reduction. His public speeches, essays and interviews frequently explore scientific innovation, public health, climate change and education, often returning to the belief that information creates greater value when it is shared widely and applied for the public good.The idea behind the featured quote reaches far beyond technology companies or research laboratories. A workplace functions more effectively when experienced staff explain systems rather than keeping specialist knowledge to themselves. Schools depend on teachers passing on understanding in ways that encourage students to think independently instead of simply memorising facts.The same principle appears in everyday life. Parents teach children practical skills. Friends exchange advice gained through experience. Communities become stronger when people willingly share information that helps others solve problems or avoid mistakes.Knowledge-sharing also benefits the person doing the teaching. Explaining an idea often exposes gaps in one's own understanding and encourages further learning. Conversations rarely move in only one direction.Digital technology has changed how information travels. Online courses, research databases, educational videos and collaborative platforms allow people to learn from experts across the world without leaving home.Greater access, however, also creates new responsibilities. Reliable information now competes with rumours, misinformation and incomplete explanations. Sharing knowledge carries value only when accuracy, evidence and clarity remain priorities.That makes the quote particularly relevant. It is not simply about making information available. It is about contributing knowledge that helps others understand the world more clearly and make informed decisions.Some readers interpret the quote as meaning that all knowledge should always be freely available. That stretches the idea further than the words themselves suggest. Privacy, intellectual property, medical confidentiality and national security all place legitimate limits on what should be shared.The central message is simpler. Knowledge creates its greatest influence when it helps other people learn, solve problems or build upon existing ideas. Real power comes not from keeping useful information out of reach, but from allowing it to become part of a wider exchange that benefits many rather than a few.
Article Summary: Bill Gates co-founded Microsoft in 1975 alongside Paul Allen. He became known for his focus on software, long-term technological trends and the rapid expansion of personal computers. His words emphasise that only sharing knowledge can give an expert an opportunity to make his contribution to the development of other people.

Article Title: Microsoft ‘breaks’ Nvidia’s record, registers biggest one-day gain in stock market history
Article Text:
Microsoft Cloud growth drives surge



Putting Microsoft’s latest numbers in perspective



Microsoft made stock market history this week by achieving the largest single-day gain in market value ever recorded by a publicly traded company, according to a report by Bloomberg. Shares of the software giant, based in Redmond, Washington, skyrocketed 16%, marking Microsoft’s biggest percentage gain since October 2008. The surge added approximately $450 billion to the company’s total market capitalisation in just one day of trading.Bloomberg says that this historic move eclipses the previous record held by Nvidia, which added $440 billion in value following an announcement regarding tariff pauses last year.The massive jump in investor confidence followed Microsoft’s latest earnings report wherein the company revealed that revenue for its Azure cloud computing unit surged 43% during the fiscal fourth quarter. This represents Microsoft Azure's fastest growth rate since early 2022, signaling strong demand for the tech giant’s cloud services.Additionally, Microsoft reassured investors by stating that its capital spending plans for 2026 remain unchanged.The nearly half-a-trillion-dollar increase in value is larger than the entire market capitalisation of roughly 96% of the companies listed on the S&P 500 index.To put it in simpler words, the value Microsoft added in one day (on July 30) alone is greater than the combined total value of the 41 smallest companies on that benchmark index – a group that includes well-known brands like Domino’s Pizza, Clorox and Hasbro.Furthermore, Microsoft’s single-day growth dwarfs the entire stock markets of several nations. The total value of all stocks traded in countries such as South Africa, Turkey, Finland and Vietnam is less than what the software maker added to its value in one day.
Article Summary: Microsoft made stock market history this week by achieving the largest single- day gain in market value ever recorded by a publicly traded company. Shares of the software giant, based in Redmond, Washington, skyrocketed 16%, marking Microsoft’s biggest percentage gain since October 2008. Article Title: Canada updates Study Permit rules, says: An officer shall not issue visa unless these conditions are met
Article Text:
Canada's new rules direct immigration officers to examine both the amount and source of an applicant’s fund

Canada tightens financial checks for study permit applicants

How much money do Canada study permit applicants need



Canada has updated its instructions for assessing study permit applications, introducing closer checks on whether international students have enough money to support themselves during their studies. The updated guidance, dated July 24, 2026, directs immigration officers to examine both the amount and source of an applicant’s funds. As per the new rules, officers may also review additional financial and employment documents to determine whether applicants are genuine students who can support themselves for the full duration of their programme. However, Canada has not changed the minimum amount of money applicants are required to show under the updated study permit rules.According to the updated “Study permits: Assessing the application” instructions, officers must assess the source of funds in all cases. The guidance also says reviewing and verifying additional individual or family financial and employment documents may be necessary.The change makes the assessment broader than under the previous instructions. Earlier guidance suggested that additional financial documents may need closer examination in “some very high-risk environments.”That qualification has now been removed.Officers can also ask applicants to provide additional supporting documents based on the facts of an individual application.The updated instructions suggest applicants may provide six months of bank statements, including the month or the month before the application was submitted. The previous guidance referred to four months of bank statements.The government has also added pension income and income from rental properties as examples of financial documents that can be used as proof of funds. An earlier example referring to a bank draft convertible into Canadian dollars has been removed. For students applying to extend their study permits, officers have been instructed to assess the required funds based on the first year following the extension.The update does not change the amount of financial support that international students must demonstrate. Applicants will still need to show that they have enough money to cover their tuition fees, travel expenses and living costs. The required amount depends on factors including family size, whether the student plans to study in Quebec and the immigration programme under which the application is made.For a single applicant studying outside Quebec under the standard study permit stream, the living-expense requirement is C$22,895, in addition to tuition and travel costs, according to the information provided.Under the Canadian immigration rules, an officer cannot issue a study permit unless the foreign national meets the applicable requirements. The tougher financial assessment means applicants may now face greater scrutiny over not only how much money they have, but also where that money came from and whether it can support them during their studies.
Article Summary: Canada's new rules direct immigration officers to examine both the amount and source of an applicant’s fund. Officers may also review additional financial and employment documents to determine whether applicants are genuine students who can support themselves. The update does not change the amount of financial support that international students must demonstrate.

Article Title: Bill Gates' daughter Phoebe Gates' shopping app Phia is in damage control mode after revelations that 'shocked' many
Article Text:
Phia claimed sales it never drove. Now it is paying brands back

Phia cookie stuffing explained: how fake clicks let a shopping app claim commissions it never earned

Phia calls it a bug, investigation calls it auto_drop: the December 2025 code that ran for seven months

Impact.com suspends Phia as refunds begin, while Phoebe Gates and Sophia Kianni say nothing

Phia, the shopping app co-founded by Phoebe Gates and Sophia Kianni, is now issuing refunds and reversing transactions after admitting it collected commissions on sales it never actually drove. Business Insider reported that the startup is working with affiliate network Impact.com to correct attributions, and a Phia spokesperson confirmed the company has offered transaction reversals to brands. Impact.com said it is reprocessing every action credited to Phia between June 20 and July 29 that had not yet been paid out, reattributing them to the right publisher or refunding advertisers.The cleanup follows a Bloomberg investigation published on July 9 that found Phia's mobile browser extension quietly opening a background tab during checkout and injecting its own referral code, overwriting whoever had actually sent the shopper there. Bloomberg tested the extension across more than 50 retail sites, including Walmart, Nike and Zara. In one test, clicking a Nordstrom link from a Wirecutter article triggered a background tab that swapped Wirecutter's affiliate code for Phia's.The practice has a name in the industry: cookie stuffing, or forced clicks.Affiliate marketing runs on one rule, that a commission is owed only when a user actually clicks a link and then buys. Independent researcher Ben Edelman, who reviewed Phia's public code and ran his own tests, found a setting called enable_coupon_auto_drop that fired affiliate links without any user action, usually at the cart or checkout page. Crucially, it was switched on only for iOS users through a server-side feature flag, which is why desktop-only testers missed it for months.Capital One Shopping, which makes a rival extension, reached the same conclusion and emailed retailers with video evidence. Publishers were losing real revenue, the email said, and advertisers were paying for fake clicks.Phia has called it a bug. Its spokesperson told Bloomberg the company learned that a recent release was causing misattributions from a subset of users, and that the team worked overnight to fix it. Bloomberg retested after contacting the company on July 7 and found the automatic referral claims had stopped.Edelman disputes the framing. The feature first shipped in version 1.9.33 on December 13, 2025, which puts it in the field for roughly seven months, including the holiday shopping season. A feature named auto_drop that automatically drops affiliate cookies, he argues, is hard to describe as an accident.The stakes are high for a company that has raised $43.5 million from Kleiner Perkins, Khosla Ventures and Notable Capital, plus celebrity backers including Hailey Bieber, Khloe Kardashian, Sydney Sweeney and Sheryl Sandberg. Phia's app has been downloaded over 1.2 million times in the past year.Impact.com has temporarily suspended Phia from its marketplace, the tool brands use to find new partners, and wants a stretch of clean compliance before reinstating it. Rakuten Advertising says it is investigating. CJ Affiliate told partners it is making reconciliation payments.Gates and Kianni, who promote Phia constantly across social media and host a podcast called The Burnouts, have said nothing publicly.
Article Summary: Phia's mobile browser extension quietly opened a background tab during checkout and injected its own referral code, overwriting whoever had actually sent the shopper there. Bloomberg tested the extension across more than 50 retail sites, including Walmart, Nike and Zara. The practice has a name in the industry: cookie stuffing, or forced clicks.

Article Title: AI has drawn Google, Meta and other tech companies into construction business, making these jobs one of the highest-paid
Article Text:
Why Google and Meta are spending millions to train electricians

A training centre caught in the middle

The massive appetite for AI’s computing power is turning construction into one of the best-paying trades in the US. Google, Meta and other tech giants are now pouring hundreds of millions of dollars into training the electricians and skilled workers needed to build their data centres, a report has said.For example, one of the data centers being built in Detroit, backed by OpenAI, is being called the single biggest private investment in Michigan's history, as per a report by The New York Times, it needs hundreds of electricians working 10-hour shifts, seven days a week, and it's paying accordingly.The pull of data centre money is the main topic of conversation at the Detroit Electrical Industry Training Center, where roughly 850 apprentices are currently training, the report added. It's one of 270 such centers across the country now getting direct support from AI companies, who are pouring hundreds of millions of dollars into making sure there are enough skilled workers to build their facilities.Meanwhile, Google alone has put in $50 million through a partnership with the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, aimed at nearly doubling the union's annual apprenticeship intake from 19,500 to 30,000 over the next three years, at locations Google has picked out itself.Asset management giant BlackRock has chipped in with its own grant as part of a separate $100 million push to widen training pipelines for its data centers in Texas.The report notes that the data centre growth is starting to squeeze everything around it: land and raw materials and workers. According to an analysis by the job site Indeed, hourly installation and maintenance jobs at data centers now pay 42% more than comparable roles in other industries.In hotspots like Dallas and Northern Virginia, where data centre construction is especially dense, workers can jump between projects for bigger bonuses or higher daily rates, and contractors are increasingly turning to staffing agencies like Aerotek just to keep crews fully staffed.Tech companies training their own workforce isn't newThis isn't the first time a tech company has taken on the job of training the people who keep its facilities running. Microsoft has been doing something similar since 2018, when it launched its own data center technician training programs. It now runs 39 such locations worldwide and has trained roughly 15,000 people through them.
Article Summary: Google, Meta and other tech giants are pouring millions into training electricians and skilled workers needed to build their data centres. Google alone has put in $50 million through a partnership with the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers. BlackRock has chipped in with its own $100 million push to widen training pipelines for its data centers in Texas.

Article Title: Google rolls back satellite image AI tool in less than 24 hours after launch, says: We have also seen people sharing screenshots
Article Text:
Google

What Google said on rolling back the feature



Experts warning to Google on Google Earth feature



In less than a day after Google unveiled a new feature that allowed users to create AI-generated satellite images with the click of a button on its Google Earth platform, the company announced it was removing the tool. Google has rolled back the new feature that allowed Google Earth users to generate AI visualizations on top of the service's satellite imagery. The roll back comes in lass than 24 hours after concerns from researchers and open-source intelligence experts about disinformation risks that the feature raised. The "create image" tool, rolled out Thursday (July 30), integrates Google's Nano Banana 2 image-generation technology to let users zoom into locations and build images in seconds based on Google Earth satellite, aerial and 3D-mapping data.In its initial announcement of the new feature on Thursday, the company said it was designed to work with users' imaginations: "Just zoom in to a place in Google Earth on web (sic), tap 'create image,' and type whatever you want to see," Bryan Horowitz, a product manager wrote.In a statement announcing the company's decision to pause the feature, Google said, "We know that people uniquely trust Google Earth for a reliable view of the world.We’ve seen geospatial professionals using this feature for a range of useful purposes, however we’ve also seen people sharing screenshots of generated imagery that appear to violate our policies. So we’re rolling back this feature in Google Earth while we work on implementing stronger guardrails. It's important to note that generated images didn’t appear in the main Google Earth experience for others to see and were watermarked as AI generated."Raising alarm on the feature, Henk van Ess, an open-source researcher, wrote on X, "I tried refugees at the Mexican border, a nuclear plant in Iran, a crash in Amsterdam, a hospital with a bomb crater in Gaza. Nothing was refused." Brady Africk, a research analyst at the American Enterprise Institute specializing in satellite imagery analysis, told AFP the Google Earth update "makes it easier to generate convincing fake satellite imagery that can spread quickly online and mislead the public. " "These AI-generated fakes, growing more common, may also erode public trust in satellite imagery, and make the jobs of journalists and researchers more difficult."In a response to AFP and Ess on X, Google said that the images created with the feature include SynthID digital watermarks, invisible markers embedded in media generated using the company's artificial intelligence tools. Users can ask Google's Gemini chatbot if a SynthID is present. "We take misinformation seriously – every image created with Nano Banana in Google Earth includes the SynthID digital watermark, so if someone is unsure about an image, they can ask the Gemini app or use Lens in Search to see if the image was AI-generated. In addition, we prevent image creation on harmful topics and are continually updating our protections," wrote Google.
Article Summary: Google has rolled back a new feature that allowed Google Earth users to generate AI visualizations on top of the service's satellite imagery. The roll back comes in lass than 24 hours after concerns from researchers and open-source intelligence experts about disinformation risks. Google said that the images created with the feature include SynthID digital watermarks.

Article Title: When a district in Florida's Everglades used robot rabbits to eliminate its ever-growing population of Burmese pythons
Article Text:
Image credit: Florida Phyton Challenge website

"Scientists from the South Florida Water Management District (District) and the University of Florida have teamed up to use robotic rabbit decoys as part of our continuing efforts to combat and remove invasive pythons."

How AI-powered robot rabbits work

Why Florida is targeting Burmese pythons

How the robot rabbits complements annual python hunt

"These innovative robots produce a heat signature and emit a smell designed to attract pythons. The robots are equipped with cameras that monitor for pythons and notify District officials when a snake is detected. Once notified, the District can dispatch a python removal agent to the area,”

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support the ongoing use of competitions like the Florida Python Challenge to control invasive species? Yes, it raises awareness and engages the community No, I prefer more scientific approaches 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Florida held its annual Python Challenge just a few weeks ago. The 10-day competition brings together professional and amateur hunters to track and remove invasive Burmese pythons from the Everglades, with cash prizes awarded for capturing the most snakes and the longest python. While the event remains one of the state's biggest efforts to control the invasive species, officials are increasingly turning to technology to find snakes that often remain hidden, and the state continues to battle its growing population of Burmese pythons.Last year, the South Florida Water Management District turned to an unusual technology after the annual Florida Python Challenge: solar-powered robot rabbits. Explaining the initiative, the district said in 2025,Designed to mimic real rabbits using artificial intelligence (AI), heat-signature and scent-simulation technologies, the devices lure pythons out of hiding and alert officials when a snake is detected.Unlike traditional wildlife monitoring tools, the robotic rabbits are designed to imitate real prey. The solar-powered, remote-controlled devices produce both a heat signature and a scent intended to attract Burmese pythons, which rely on thermal sensing and smell while hunting.Each robot is equipped with an AI-powered camera that continuously monitors its surroundings. When the system detects a python approaching, it automatically alerts officials at the South Florida Water Management District. A trained python removal agent is then dispatched to capture and remove the snake.According to the district, the robots are strategically deployed across South Florida at locations where pythons are known to hide, allowing officials to monitor areas that are otherwise difficult to survey.The robot rabbits are the latest addition to Florida's long-running efforts to control Burmese pythons, which were introduced into the wild decades ago and have become one of the Everglades' dominant invasive predators.Conservationists estimate there are between 100,000 and 300,000 Burmese pythons across Florida's subtropical regions. Adult females can lay more than 70 eggs in a single clutch, while the snakes can grow to more than 18 feet long.According to the South Florida Water Management District, invasive pythons prey on native mammals, birds and reptiles, reducing food sources for species including Florida panthers, bobcats and birds of prey.The impact has been documented by the US Geological Survey, whose 2012 study found raccoon and opossum populations in parts of the Everglades had declined by nearly 99% following the spread of Burmese pythons.Before deploying robotic rabbits, Florida primarily relied on trained contractors and public participation through the annual Florida Python Challenge.The 10-day competition brings together professional and amateur snake hunters to remove invasive pythons from the Everglades. Participants must complete a safety course before taking part, and all captured snakes must be euthanised using methods approved by the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission.More than 600 people had registered for this year’s challenge before it began, while over 900 local and international competitors participated in this year's event.According to the South Florida Water Management District, more than 19,000 Burmese pythons have been removed from the Everglades since 2000 through state removal programmes and public initiatives. Last year, the district said the robotic rabbit programme is intended to complement those efforts rather than replace them.the district noted.
Article Summary: Scientists from the South Florida Water Management District (District) and the University of Florida have teamed up to use robotic rabbit decoys. The robots produce a heat signature and emit a smell designed to attract pythons. Each robot is equipped with an AI-powered camera that continuously monitors its surroundings. When the system detects a python approaching, it automatically alerts officials.

Article Title: In 1599, this foundry started making church bells; now it's using 3D printing to preserve 400 year old tradition
Article Text:
Image credit: X (Twitter)

"Certain things are just like they were 400 years ago. But we innovated a lot. Especially within the last 20 years, we've changed a lot."

Traditional casting meets modern technology

Precision remains essential during casting

"The important thing is that you have to calculate, form and then cast the bell as a musical instrument,"

Rising costs and changing demand

"That's why I can't even say how much a bell is going to cost in a year. I just hope the metal price is going to come down again,"

Restoration work helps preserve the craft

"This bell is for the church in Zethau, in Germany. I'm very happy with the casting. I'm especially happy that the innovations of the past decades helped a lot to make the bells ever more beautiful and better,”

One of Europe's last surviving bell foundries is combining centuries-old craftsmanship with modern technologies to keep a tradition dating back more than 400 years alive. At the Grassmayr Bell Foundry in Innsbruck, Austria, artisans continue to cast bronze church bells using techniques passed down through generations, while also relying on 3D printing, laser technology and computer simulations to improve production.Founded in 1599, the family-run foundry is now managed by brothers Johannes and Peter Grassmayr. Explaining how the business has evolved, Johannes Grassmayr told the news agency AP,Workers at the foundry wear protective equipment as they pour molten bronze into specially designed moulds reinforced with steel bands to produce bells weighing several tonnes. The current production includes 12 bells destined for churches in Italy, Germany and Romania.While the overall production cycle still takes three to four months, technology has shortened several stages of the process. According to Johannes Grassmayr, cleaning and polishing a newly cast bell once accounted for nearly 30% of production time. With modern equipment, the same work now takes about one-tenth as long.The foundry also uses technologies including 3D printing, 3D scanning, laser systems, and specialised computer applications to calculate the sound characteristics of each bell. Some production techniques, including a high-pressure sandblasting chamber used for cleaning, remain proprietary.Despite technological advances, creating the mould for a large bell can still take up to six months.Johannes said, adding that the greatest challenge is ensuring the mould withstands the pressure created during casting.According to the foundry, molten bronze inside a mould for a multi-tonne bell can generate up to 125 metric tonnes of pressure. To withstand those forces, workers use high-quality clay moulds enclosed within specially designed steel sleeves.The foundry is also facing business challenges beyond manufacturing. Johannes Grassmayr said demand has been affected as fewer churches are being built across Europe. At the same time, energy prices have increased following the war in Ukraine, while labour costs have risen by around 30% since the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.Material costs have also climbed sharply. According to Johannes, the price of bronze, which is made from 80% copper and 20% tin, has increased from about 8 euros per kilogram a few years ago to around 23 euros per kilogram today.he said.To adapt to changing demand, the Grassmayr family has expanded its restoration business, repairing defective bells using modern technology. According to the company, it has restored hundreds of bells from 12 European countries.Grassmayr bells are installed in more than 100 countries. Among the foundry's largest projects is a bell cast in 2016 for Romania's National Cathedral in Bucharest, measuring 3.3 metres tall and weighing more than 25 metric tonnes. Another 15-metric-tonne bell hangs in a church on Mount Tabor in Israel.Showing recently cast bells cooling inside their moulds, Johannes pointed to the detailed imprint left in the clay.he said.
Article Summary: Grassmayr Bell Foundry in Innsbruck, Austria, was founded in 1599. Artisans continue to cast bronze church bells using techniques passed down through generations. The foundry also uses 3D printing, laser technology and computer simulations to improve production.

Article Text:
Google, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta AI spending cross $1 trillion mark

AI hyperscalers’ $745 billion pipeline and shrinking cash flow



Nearly $900 billion in new commitments



Tech giants Google , Amazon, Microsoft and Meta have cumulatively poured more than $1 trillion into capital investments since the race for artificial intelligence (AI) dominance kicked off three and a half years ago. The spending spree, however, is beginning to rattle Wall Street as free cash flow drops to lows and timeline expectations stretch out for years, as per a report by The Financial Times. According to earnings reports released over the past two weeks, combined capital expenditure across the four hyperscalers reached $1.1 trillion between the start of the AI boom in 2023 and the end of June.The outlay shows no signs of slowing. Driven by escalating projections from Google and Amazon, the four companies plan to spend an additional $745 billion this year, primarily on specialised data centres, advanced semiconductors and the power capacity required to run them.The report says that the combined free cash flow for the four tech giants fell to a decade-low of just $7 billion in the recent quarter, with only Microsoft and Meta bringing in more cash than they spent. Google even recorded its first quarter of negative free cash flow since going public over two decades ago, posting a negative $6 billion for the period.Rishi Jaluria, an RBC Capital analyst, noted that there is essentially no end in sight for capex growth, adding that investors need these firms to toe a tight line between funding AI and preserving the profitability that made them successful in the first place.The scale of long-term financial obligations is expanding rapidly. Google added $500 billion in future financial commitments linked to long-term infrastructure and data center energy deals.Meta signed $233 billion in new commitments, including $96 billion in data centre leases, $112 billion in cloud capacity purchases, and another $68 billion in leases added in July. Similarly, Microsoft agreed to more than $130 billion in new data centre leases during the second quarter alone.Together, Google, Meta, and Microsoft added nearly $900 billion in new AI-related obligations in a single three-month window.Meanwhile, investors are growing far less forgiving of heavy spenders without immediate monetisation routes. As per Dec Mullarkey, managing director at SLC Management, investors no longer accept growth at any cost and want to see spending flow directly into financial results.The massive capital rotation is also straining global supply chains. A severe shortage of memory chips has driven up hardware costs across the tech sector, impacting companies like Apple even as it sits outside the central cloud infrastructure battle.
Article Summary: Google, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta AI spending cross $1 trillion mark. Free cash flow for the four tech giants fell to a decade-low of just $7 billion in the recent quarter. Google even recorded its first quarter of negative free cash flow since going public over two decades ago.
